correctness.rationale: PASS for the corrected presentation under repairs/2. The original boxed identity was correct, but the accompanying p(p+1) summand count at RESULT.md lines 62 and 78 was false. There are p+1 options on each side, including the no-zero sentinels. Indeed all (p+1)^2 indexed terms can be nonzero: if each class has size at least two, place one zero in each prescribed frontier class and label every other vertex two. Every nonempty monitored prefix or suffix then has weight at least two. In particular p=2 and all sizes two gives nine nonzero terms, not six. In the repaired proof the first zero in A and last zero in B uniquely specify their frontier classes. Nested neighborhoods and nonnegative weights mean defending the two tightest zero-class neighborhoods is necessary and sufficient. The polynomials U,V,W independently count named-vertex labels with, respectively, arbitrary labels, all positive labels, and at least one zero. The two truncations remove precisely the degree-0 and degree-1 choices on the required opposite-side prefix and suffix (or are omitted for absent frontiers). Multiplying disjoint side choices and summing disjoint frontier cells gives the exact all-weight polynomial, including the p=1 boundary. Independent local-rule enumeration and frontier polynomial comparison (`python3 -B /workspace/branches/bounded_review_checks.py 2`) verified 74 distinct ordered profiles, 1111 profile/frontier cells and 754254 assignments; it also independently verified both weight-four examples (minimum 4, counts 4 and 6). The frozen script was read, not executed. It has two repeated nine-vertex profiles ((1,2,1),(2,1,2)) and its reversal, explaining its 76 list entries, 1143 comparisons and 793620 assignments with repeats. The corrected RESULT.md, REVIEW.md, and verification notes distinguish these counts, preserve the original verification front matter, and leave all frozen evidence intact. Finite checks do not substitute for the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: The repaired identity gives the entire weight distribution for a natural graph class with arbitrary class multiplicities, including many cyclic examples, where knowing a minimum is not enough. The proof reduces feasibility on potentially many zero vertices to two weight conditions and compresses the count to (p+1)^2 product-and-truncation cells. The independently checked equal-minimum but unequal-coefficient examples illustrate concrete information beyond optimization. This is valuable as a direct structural formula, not a claim to the first general automatic counting algorithm.
